title: Wheel plants a .pth import hook, credential stealer, and sitecustomize remote loader under .data/purelib
provenance: LiteLLM 1.107.0 (PyPI + Docker, 2026-10-21): the project's own release workflow built from a lookalike source repository; [tool.maturin] data = "cook" copied cook.pth (import cook), cook.py (env/cloud credential stealer posting to an attacker healthcheck URL) and sitecustomize.py (hourly dead-drop loader that exec()s fetched code) into site-packages via the wheel's .data/purelib scheme, so every interpreter start ran them without importing the package. Sources: StepSecurity and Socket incident write-ups. Defanged: renamed to a fictional model-gateway project, hosts replaced with example.invalid, env var names only (no values), loader body reduced to the fetch-and-exec shape.
intent: Models the startup-hook persistence and credential exfil of the 1.107.0 wheels against a clean 1.106.2 baseline. Drydock should land high on the release delta via pypi.pth-execution and pypi.startup-hook at the .data/purelib install root, plus credential/network/dynamic-eval code findings. Safe: inert JSON evidence, example.invalid hosts, no secrets.
